rows.n: data cleaning
rows.b: Removing junk, duplicates, and garbage from training text so the model learns from quality material.

rows.n: data contamination
rows.b: When test questions leak into training data, making benchmark scores look better than they really are.

rows.n: data epoch
rows.b: One complete pass over the training data, after which shuffling usually starts a fresh order.

rows.n: data loader
rows.b: The code that streams training examples from disk into the GPU fast enough to keep it busy.

rows.n: data mixture
rows.b: The recipe of how much web text, books, code, and other sources go into the training corpus.

rows.n: data parallel
rows.b: Splitting batches across many GPUs that each hold a full copy of the model and sync their updates.

rows.n: dataset
rows.b: An organized collection of examples used to train or test a model.

rows.n: decoder
rows.b: The transformer half that generates output one token at a time, each step looking back at what it already wrote.

rows.n: decoder-only model
rows.b: A language model built from decoders alone, which predicts the next token — the design behind Signature Llama and most chat models.

rows.n: deduplication
rows.b: Deleting repeated passages from training data, since heavy repetition teaches the model to parrot.

rows.n: deployment
rows.b: Putting a trained model where real users can reach it — the trip from lab to the world.

rows.n: deterministic decoding
rows.b: Generation settings, like temperature zero, that produce the same output every time for the same input.

rows.n: detokenization
rows.b: Converting the model's output token IDs back into readable text.

rows.n: distillation
rows.b: Training a small student model to imitate a big teacher, keeping most of the quality at a fraction of the size.

rows.n: Docker
rows.b: The standard container tool for shipping software, models included, with identical environments.

rows.n: document
rows.b: One coherent piece of text in the corpus, like an article or a dictionary entry.

rows.n: DPO
rows.b: Direct preference optimization — a simpler way to teach human preferences that skips the separate reward model RLHF needs.

rows.n: dropout
rows.b: A training trick that randomly switches off some neurons, forcing the network to not lean on any single one.
